errors.why: dbugs dbyung here is ucchvāsa, 'chapter/section': the ritual condenses the six chapters (of the Māyājāla material), not 'six types of relief'.

note: Title, homage verses and opening ritual instructions are rendered faithfully apart from the technical sense of dbugs dbyung.

errors.english: do not perish or cease; if they were to undergo change, as it is said,
errors.why: Parallel to the preceding lemma, the sūtra says those things have been exhausted, have ceased, are nonexistent and have changed, which is why the commentary says it shows their nonexistence.

fix.find: do not perish or cease; if they were to undergo change, as it is said,
fix.replace: have been exhausted, have ceased and do not exist, having changed" and so forth,

note: Generally follows the commentary on rejoicing and dedication well, but one lemma has its meaning inverted.

errors.english: Having become a great scholar, and in order to produce the nectar that counteracts poison as described in the Tantras, he took on the appearance of a peacock.
errors.why: The one who became a great scholar and adopted peacock attire is the younger brother sent to the scholars (cf. mkhas pas below), not the yogi-raised elder brother as the English implies.

note: The narrative of the two brothers and the refutation of the standing-vow is clear and mostly accurate.
Careful, terminologically consistent rendering of the sixteen forsakings and the lemmata on emptiness yoga.

errors.why: In this death-deceiving computation nyi ma means days (the count of days), not the sun.

note: The numerical diagram procedure is followed closely; some Kālacakra calendrical terms are rendered too literally.
Faithful rendering of the commentary on the hundredfold powers and the transition to the ten bhūmis.
Accurate rendering of the commentary on the elements as the goddesses and on beings as buddhas.

errors.english: Not only is this translated here
errors.why: 'gyur ba here means the offense 'occurs/comes about', not 'is translated'.

fix.find: Not only is this translated here
fix.replace: Not only does the offense occur here

errors.why: 'og ma means 'the following' training rules, of which the first is the threatening gesture (gzas pa); the English fuses the list heading into the first item.
Mūlasarvāstivāda Vinaya is in the Sanskrit tradition: the grave offense (gnas ngan len, dauṣṭhulya) is a saṅghāvaśeṣa, not the Pali form.

fix.replace: Sanskrit: dauṣṭhulya, i.e. a saṅghāvaśeṣa offense

errors.english: refers to the intention to strike another person
errors.why: The commentary says the 'other' thing to be struck is the mind (one should discipline the mind, not strike one's body).

fix.find: refers to the intention to strike another person
fix.replace: means that what is to be struck is the mind

note: The casuistry of striking is mostly followed, but several Vinaya points are garbled, including the key gloss on what is to be struck.

errors.english: the eight pillars of the (mandala) sacred circle
errors.why: 'khor lo la sogs pa means the eight pillars marked with the wheel and other emblems, not 'pillars of the mandala'.

note: The eight liberations and the symbolism of the palace are rendered well, with some loosening of the long descriptive compound.

errors.english: "Without going outside, they shall be separated in this manner like two travelers."
errors.why: The source says one should not send the guest ('dron pa) outside but divide the space in two with the guest; there is no 'like two travelers' and no one 'going outside'.

note: The rules on sleeping with the unordained are clear and accurate apart from the garbled source citation.
